This sequence is clinically relevant as it shows the transition from surgical intervention to post-operative pain management.
answer:
1. Incision and Drainage with Malecot Placement  
   - On the day of surgery, the patient was taken to the OR under general anesthesia for incision and drainage of his perirectal abscess.  
   - Nearly 1 L of purulent fluid was evacuated. The previously placed drain was removed and a new Malecot drain was secured.  
   - He tolerated the procedure well and was extubated in recovery.  

2. Early Post-Op Management  
   - Post-op Day 1: He spiked a fever to 101.6 °F and received acetaminophen 1 g IV. A chest X-ray showed no pneumonia. Blood cultures were obtained (pending), and empiric Unasyn was started after gram stain showed gram-positive cocci.  

3. De-escalation of Antibiotics  
   - After adequate source control via drainage, Unasyn was discontinued. Wound cultures grew mixed flora, but no further systemic antibiotics were felt necessary.  

4. Transition to Oral Pain Control and Discharge  
   - His pain was controlled post-op with acetaminophen and ibuprofen. On discharge, he was prescribed oxycodone IR 5 mg PO every 4 hours as needed for breakthrough pain, along with acetaminophen 650 mg PO Q6 H PRN, to ensure adequate analgesia at home.  

Clinical relevance of this sequence  
   - Effective source control (I&D and drain placement) is the cornerstone of managing perirectal abscesses and allows safe discontinuation of broad-spectrum antibiotics.  
   - Transitioning from IV antipyretics and empiric antibiotics to targeted—or no—antibiotics minimizes drug exposure and resistance risk.  
   - A stepwise approach to pain management (nonopioid → short-term opioid) balances adequate analgesia against opioid-related side effects (e.g., constipation) and supports early mobilization and return of bowel function.

  • TIPS occlusion and portal vein thrombosis – the thrombectomy, thrombolysis and stent revision restored flow through the shunt and portal system.  
  • Variceal bleeding from portal hypertension – the embolization and sclerotherapy directly treated his high-risk gastric/coronary varices.
